draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Athirappilly! The Chalakudy river drops about 25 metres here, and in the monsoon the falls go wide and roaring. People call it the Niagara of India.
draft.hungryLine: Food here is roadside and simple: tea, snacks and meals on the way to the falls.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk to the top of the falls, then take the path down to the bottom for the full view.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit on the rocks above the falls and just listen.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Four kinds of hornbill live in these forests. Look up when you hear a heavy wingbeat.

legends.title: Famous on film
legends.body: These falls have starred in many films. If they look familiar, you may have seen them in Baahubali.

legends.title: The bird of the forest
legends.body: The great hornbill is Kerala's state bird. The forests around here are one of the best places to spot one.

tips.title: Monsoon is the big show.
tips.body: July to September is the loudest, but the path is slippery.

tips.title: Keep the plastic.
tips.body: The area is plastic-free. Bags may be checked at the gate.

story.title: A river in the forest
story.body: The Chalakudy river runs down from the Western Ghats through some of Kerala's richest forest.

story.title: The Kadar people
story.body: The Kadar community has lived in these forests for generations, gathering honey and forest produce.

story.title: A popular escape
story.body: Families from Thrissur and Kochi began driving out for a day by the falls.

story.title: A fight for the river
story.body: A hydroelectric dam was proposed just above the falls. Many people campaigned against it to protect the river and the forest.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Top of the falls, bottom of the falls, then Vazhachal. Tell me how wet you got.
